official_source_evidence.finding: Official docs state validators publish spot oracle prices for each perp asset approximately every 3 seconds and the final clearinghouse oracle is the stake-weighted median of validator submissions. The page does not expose the native publish action/message schema or historical serialization mapping.

Official docs identify s3://hl-mainnet-node-data/explorer_blocks and s3://hl-mainnet-node-data/replica_cmds as historical explorer blocks and L1 transactions, respectively, and state requester-paid transfer costs apply. No native-oracle mapping is documented.
Official L1 schema docs identify replica_cmds as transaction blocks at ~/hl/data/replica_cmds/{start_time}/{date}/{height}. No native validator-oracle transaction/action schema is documented.

Official node README documents --replica-cmds-style actions/actions-and-responses and separately documents --write-hip3-oracle-updates for HIP-3 deployer oracle actions. It does not identify a native BTC/ETH validator-oracle action/schema in replica_cmds.

official_source_evidence.finding: Searches for oracle/validatorL1/replica_cmds exposed HIP-3 setOracle/deployer update APIs and read-side oraclePx fields, but no public native validator-oracle publish action/message schema. This absence evidence is supportive only and is not treated as proof that historical raw bytes lack such data.

hip3_identity_guard.reason: HIP-3 deployer oracle updates are a distinct builder/deployer mechanism and cannot be substituted for the validator-operated native BTC/ETH oracle.

interpretation: Official public sources establish the economic role and cadence of the native validator oracle and establish that replica_cmds stores L1 transaction blocks, but they do not publicly expose an unambiguous native validator-oracle publish message/action schema nor an explicit mapping of that schema into replica_cmds/explorer_blocks. P0D therefore fails its frozen public-schema identity gate. This does not prove the raw requester-pays node-history bytes lack reconstructable oracle state; that remains an access-blocked source question.
